questions.question: Which group of the periodic table contains the noble gases, which are known for being unreactive?
options: Group 1
Group 7
Group 0
Group 2

questions.question: What is the physical state of all noble gases at room temperature?
options: Liquid
Gas
Solid
Some are solids and some are gases

questions.question: Why are the noble gases chemically stable and unreactive?
options: They have complete outer electron shells.
They have no electrons in their outer shell.
They easily lose one electron.
They have an odd number of protons.

questions.question: As you move down Group 0 in the periodic table, how do the physical properties of the elements change?
options: Atomic mass decreases, density decreases, and boiling points increase.
Atomic mass, density, and boiling points all increase.
Atomic mass increases, density decreases, and boiling points decrease.
Atomic mass, density, and boiling points all decrease.

questions.question: How do the chemical and physical properties of elements within any given group generally change as you go down the group?
options: They change randomly from one element to the next.
They remain completely identical for all elements.
They change gradually down the group.
They only change when moving from left to right.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the trends and properties of Group 1 metals?
options: They are hard, have very high densities, and become less reactive down the group.
They are soft, have lower densities than most other metals, and become more reactive down the group.
They are hard, have lower densities than most other metals, and become less reactive down the group.
They are soft, have very high densities, and become more reactive down the group.

questions.question: Why are Group 1 metals specifically referred to as the 'alkali metals'?
options: Because they form acidic solutions when they react with non-metals.
Because they react with water to form an alkaline solution and hydrogen gas.
Because they turn blue litmus paper red when dissolved in water.
Because they react with acids to produce salt and water only.

questions.question: What products are formed when Group 2 metals react with dilute acids?
options: An alkaline solution and oxygen gas
A metal halide and water
A salt and hydrogen gas
A salt and carbon dioxide gas

questions.question: How does the reactivity of Group 2 metals compare to Group 1 metals in the same period, and how does it change down Group 2?
options: Group 2 metals are more reactive than Group 1 metals and become less reactive down the group.
Group 2 metals are less reactive than Group 1 metals and become less reactive down the group.
Group 2 metals are more reactive than Group 1 metals and become more reactive down the group.
Group 2 metals are less reactive than Group 1 metals and become more reactive down the group.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of the elements in Group 7?
options: They are metals that form highly coloured alkaline liquids.
They are non-metals that have coloured, mostly toxic vapours.
They are unreactive gases with no colour or odour.
They are highly reflective metals that form coloured salts.

questions.question: How does the physical state of Group 7 elements at room temperature change as you go down the group?
options: It changes from gas to solid.
It changes from solid to gas.
It changes from liquid to gas.
All elements in Group 7 are gases at room temperature.

questions.question: What is the trend in reactivity as you move down Group 7 of the periodic table?
options: Reactivity increases.
Reactivity decreases.
Reactivity remains constant.
Reactivity decreases then increases.

questions.question: What is formed when halogens react with Group 1 and Group 2 metals?
options: Metal oxides
Metal hydroxides
Metal halides
Metal carbonates

questions.question: What is a common property of the metal halides formed by the reaction of halogens with Group 1 and 2 metals?
options: They are insoluble in water.
They are highly soluble in water.
They are gases at room temperature.
They are highly acidic liquids.

questions.question: In the periodic table, what are the vertical columns and horizontal rows called?
options: Columns are called periods, and rows are called groups.
Columns are called groups, and rows are called series.
Columns are called families, and rows are called periods.
Columns are called groups, and rows are called periods.

questions.question: Which Russian scientist is credited with developing the periodic table?
options: John Dalton
Dimitri Mendeleev
Marie Curie
Ernest Rutherford

questions.question: How are all the elements organized in the periodic table?
options: Alphabetically by their chemical names.
Into groups and periods according to their properties.
By the date of their discovery.
Based on their abundance in the Earth's crust.

questions.question: What is true about elements that are located in the same group of the periodic table?
options: They have completely different physical states.
They have similar chemical and physical properties.
They have the same atomic mass.
They cannot react with other elements.

questions.question: Besides being arranged into groups, how can elements in the periodic table be broadly divided?
options: Into solids and liquids only.
Into natural and artificial elements only.
Into non-metals and metals, which include the transition metals.
Into reactive gases and unreactive solids.
